title: Stockport trains resume after overhead wire damage

input.evidence_text: Train services have begun running again through Stockport after damage to overhead electrical wires caused major disruption across the rail network An empty Northern train became stranded near Stockport Viaduct shortly after midnight on Friday, blocking the line and forcing the closure of all services through the station Six train operators were affected, including Avanti West Coast, Northern and CrossCountry, with services cancelled, diverted or terminating earlier than scheduled Shortly after 09:30 BST, Network Rail said engineers had repaired the damage and reopened the lines, but warned passengers to expect further delays and cancellations while services returned to normal Photographs showed engineers using an elevated platform to reach the overhead wires as they made repairs Clare Waller, Network Rail's area director for Manchester, apologised to passengers, saying they had not received "the service they deserve or expect"

It's really shocking." The nursery was issued with a prohibition order by Salford Council's environmental health department on Friday, 2 October after inspectors discovered vermin in the Liverpool Road building. title: Warning to drivers as part of M60 to shut for gantries demolition

input.lead: Severe congestion is expected while work takes place at Simister Island on the M60 in Bury
input.summary: Severe congestion is expected while work takes place at Simister Island on the M60 in Bury
input.evidence_text: Warning to drivers as part of M60 to shut for gantries demolition - BBC News Image caption, Junction 17 and 18 of the M60 in Bury, Greater Manchester, will be shut on Saturday evening By Lynette Horsburgh North West Published 9 October 2026 Drivers are being warned of "severe congestion" when a busy stretch of motorway is closed this weekend as part of an upgrade to the road. Junction 17 and 18 of the M60 in Bury, Greater Manchester, will be shut on Saturday night until 06:00 on Monday. The closures are to enable the demolition of two large overhead gantries at the Simister Island Interchange. It comes after two others were removed last month. National Highways said the work was part of a £300m improvement scheme and would improve traffic flow, support future housing, employment and growth across the region. Frances Oliver, of National Highways, told BBC North West Tonight : "These gantries are up to 120 tonnes so it's very similar to removing a small footbridge so it is quite a large amount of work for us to undertake." Image caption, Two busy junctions at Simister and Prestwich will be closed for the work Oliver added: "We are expecting there to be severe congestion in the area so we are asking people to plan their journeys, check before they travel and if at all try not to travel or defer their journey. "The message is if you don't need to be in the area please try not to be." Image caption, Frances Oliver asked people to avoid the area while the work is taking place this weekend Full closures and timings From Saturday 10 October to Monday 12 October The M60 westbound will be closed from 22:00 on Saturday to 06:00 on Monday The M60 eastbound will be closed from 23:59 on Saturday to 06:00 on Monday Get in touch Tell us which stories we should cover in Greater Manchest

input.evidence_text: Plans for new train services between London and Wrexham, Rochdale and Blackpool have been rejected by the Office of Rail and Road (ORR) The proposal to add more trains on the West Coast Main Line would "likely increase delays and cancelled trains for passengers", the regulator said It rejected an application from Wrexham, Shropshire and Midlands Railway (WSMR) for five daily Wrexham to London Euston return services, as well as Lumo's proposal for up to four return services between Rochdale and Euston on weekdays and Saturdays, and three on Sundays Avanti West Coast's plans for additional services between Blackpool and Euston were also denied by the ORR The regulator said: "Gaps in the current timetable need to provide important space for trains to recover when disruption occurs, minimising delays to passengers "ORR concluded that adding more services into these windows in the timetable for recovery would reduce that resilience, increasing the risk of disruption spreading to other services and affecting more passengers."

input.lead: It’s been a busy week at Labour Party Conference in Liverpool, with technology, growth and devolution featuring heavily in many of the conversations we’ve been part of In his first Conference speech as Prime Minister, Andy Burnham talked about devolving more power to places, back
input.summary: It’s been a busy week at Labour Party Conference in Liverpool, with technology, growth and devolution featuring heavily in many of the conversations we’ve been part of In his first Conference speech as Prime Minister, Andy Burnham talked about devolving more power to places, back
input.evidence_text: It’s been a busy week at Labour Party Conference in Liverpool, with technology, growth and devolution featuring heavily in many of the conversations we’ve been part of In his first Conference speech as Prime Minister, Andy Burnham talked about devolving more power to places, backing businesses to grow and taking some of what has worked in Greater Manchester into a wider national approach. He also confirmed that AI will be a central focus of the That felt particularly relevant following an event we hosted through the UK Tech Cluster Group with AI Minister Kanishka Narayan, North East Mayor Kim McGuinness and other regional leaders, looking at AI, devolution and local growth One of the clearest themes from the discussion was that devolution should not mean every place trying to build the same thing. input.evidence_text: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing. As investors grow increasingly selective, the capital ecosystem has become polarised. More capital is being concentrated in fewer companies while the market for exits remains difficult Financial news recently added another dimension to that discussion. AI-related shares fell last week after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for a slower approach to the development of increasingly capable AI models. Nvidia finished the day down 3.4%, SoftBank fell 10.7% in Tokyo Additionally, the Bank of England is predicted to increase interest rates later this year, which could affect the North West's tech funding landscape by raising the cost of capital across the board, compressing valuations, pushing investors toward profitability over growth-at-all The British Business Bank's 2026 Small Business Equity Tracker found that equity investment into UK smaller businesses fell 4% to £12.3bn in 2025. Seed deal numbers fell 27% and venture deals fell 13%. AI companies attracted 44% of all investment into smaller businesses while the Beauhurst recorded £14.4bn of UK equity investment across 2,799 deals in the first half of 2026 but three AI companies accounted for 29% of all the capital raised. Those very large rounds can make the overall market look stronger than it feels to businesses raising at seed or Ser Beauhurst's analysis shows that UK equity investment more than doubled between 2017 and 2021 to £32.2bn while annual exits remained at around 400 to 500. input.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained.
